title: Radha's friend carries the news
hookLine: Radha's friend runs to Krishna: the moonlight that should cool her is burning her
carry: the sakhi's bhakti: serve a love bigger than you

lines: A FRIEND COMES WITH A REPORT.
cards: Sandal paste on the skin. Moonlight through the leaves. A soft wind off the southern hills.
In poems like this one, these are the comforts of a hot evening, the things that cool a body down. Now a friend of Radha's comes to Krishna, where he waits in the forest, with a report.
Everything that ought to soothe her, she says, is burning her. This is Radha's side, carried by someone who has just been sitting with her.

teach.h: THE MOON AND SANDAL BURN HER.
teach.b: Here's the friend's song, in paraphrase. She blames the sandal paste. She blames the rays of the moon.
They don't cool her; they torment her. The breeze from the sandalwood hills feels to her like poison. Even a bed of flowers gives her no rest.

teach.h: IN SEPARATION FROM YOU, SHE IS MISERABLE.
teach.b: And the refrain keeps returning: in separation from you, Krishna, she is miserable. That's viraha again: the moon is the same moon, but the one she loves isn't there, so every sweet thing points to him.
Now notice who is singing. Not Radha. Not Krishna.
Her friend, her sakhi. She doesn't argue Radha out of her grief, and she doesn't scold Krishna.
She sits with one, walks to the other, and tells the truth about what she saw. In Chaitanya's tradition, this friend matters enormously.
There, Radha is Krishna's own power of love, and devotees don't usually picture themselves as Radha at all.

They take the place of her friends and helpers: the ones who carry messages, prepare the bower, and are happiest when the two meet. That's a teaching about the self. The devotee's joy isn't in being the center.

teach.h: SERVE A LOVE BIGGER THAN YOU.
teach.b: It's in serving a love bigger than you: the love between Radha and Krishna.
You can see it in temple life: the cooks who make food for the deity, the singers who lead kirtan so others can come close, the ones who arrange the flowers and are never seen.
Read that way, the friend's report is a prayer, and her running feet are devotion.

how: In Vaishnava kirtan and in classical dance, the Gita Govinda is performed song by song, and the friend's report of Radha's state is one of the songs performers take up; in Chaitanya's tradition, devotees often understand their own place as that of Radha's friends and helpers, serving the love of Radha and Krishna.

o: devotion: serving a love bigger than yourself
a cooling calm that keeps every longing far away
a gift of sandal paste offered at a shrine

p: meant to cool, they burn her
in separation from you, she is miserable

s: in the friend's song, moonlight and sandal paste comfort Radha
she blames them both: in her separation, they torment her instead of cooling her.
in Chaitanya's tradition, many devotees picture themselves as Radha's friends rather than as Radha
their joy is serving the love of Radha and Krishna.
the friend scolds Krishna for what he did
she doesn't scold anyone. she tells him the truth about what she saw.

games.q: you're Radha's friend. she's in pain, and Krishna is waiting in the forest. what do you do?
o: tell Radha to get over it.
go to Krishna and tell him exactly how she is.
games.why: the friend goes to Krishna and sings Radha's state to him: everything that should cool her burns, and she is miserable without him.

practice: Feel the cool air at the edge of the nostrils for a few breaths. Then bring to mind someone whose hurt you know, someone who can't easily say it themselves.
Picture carrying their truth, gently and honestly, the way the sakhi carries Radha's to Krishna.
If you pray, carry them into your prayer now, by name, asking nothing for yourself; if you don't, hold them in mind, and ask what one honest word on their behalf would sound like.

wordCard.voice: Bhakti. Devotion. In the friend's song, it's a love that runs on someone else's errand: the sakhi serving a love bigger than herself.

orig.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: sakhi, a woman's close friend; in the Gita Govinda, Radha's friend and go-between.

carryVoice: Your line: the sakhi's bhakti, serve a love bigger than you. Day nine hundred seventy-eight, done.

sources.ref: Gita Govinda, the friend's report of Radha's longing (the song with the refrain 'sa virahe tava dina')
